title: DigitalWatchClear
question: How does a digital watch work?
hook: No gears, no hands, no ticking. A sliver of quartz, a row of counters and a sandwich of liquid crystal that twists light keep the time on one coin cell for seven years. Take a digital watch apart in 3D and count the seconds yourself.

explainer.title: A chip, a crystal, a cell and a piece of glass
explainer.text: Inside the resin case is a small module: a circuit board with one chip under a blob of black epoxy, a quartz crystal in a tiny can, and a 3 volt coin cell. The display glass has no wires. Two rubber zebra strips squeezed between board and glass carry every signal, and a piezo disc on the steel back makes the beep.

explainer.title: One tick a second
explainer.text: The quartz crystal is cut like a tuning fork and rings 32,768 times a second. That is 2 multiplied by itself 15 times, so a chain of fifteen flip-flops, each halving the beat, ends at exactly one pulse a second. Faster beats along the chain feed the beeper and the display.

explainer.title: A row of counters
explainer.text: The chip does not know the time. It counts. Seconds run 0 to 59, roll over to 0 and pass a carry to the minutes; minutes carry to hours, hours to the date. The date counter checks the month for its limit, and a watch that stores the year gives February 29 days in a leap year.

explainer.title: Seven bars make every digit
explainer.text: Each digit is kept as four bits. A decoder turns them into seven on or off signals, one for each bar of the figure of eight. A watch face can have 80 bars, so they share wires: three back electrodes take turns, and 30 chip pins do the work of 81.

explainer.title: A sandwich that twists light
explainer.text: A segment is liquid crystal between two polarisers set at right angles, over a reflector. With no voltage, the molecules form a quarter-turn twist that guides room light through both polarisers and back out: clear. About 3 volts stands the molecules up, the twist is lost, the light is blocked: dark. It makes no light of its own.

explainer.title: Four jobs on a millionth of an amp
explainer.text: The Mode button steps the chip from clock to alarm to stopwatch to setting, and the other buttons change meaning in each. An alarm is a comparator and a 4,096 Hz tone into the piezo disc. The whole watch averages about 1.5 microamps, so one coin cell lasts seven years or more. A smartwatch uses over ten thousand times as much.

concepts.def: A tiny tuning fork of quartz that the chip keeps ringing at a very steady 32,768 swings a second.
A chain of flip-flops that each halve the frequency; fifteen of them turn 32,768 Hz into one pulse a second.
A circuit that adds one for every pulse, rolls over at its limit and sends a carry to the next counter.
Binary-coded decimal: each decimal digit stored on its own as four bits, from 0000 to 1001.
A digit drawn with seven bars, named a to g. Different sets of bars make 0 to 9.
A liquid whose rod-shaped molecules share a direction and can be turned by a small voltage.
The LCD type where the molecules make a quarter-turn twist that guides light between two crossed polarisers.
Driving many segments with few wires by letting two to four back electrodes take turns, many times a second.
A circuit that is always in one of a few modes and steps between them when a button is pressed.
